reasoning_traces.think:
The taxonomy defines a hierarchical lattice of data trustworthiness through evidence tiers T1–T6. Each provider module is mapped into a category (1–7) and assigned an evidence tier. GSI uses this to construct a Bayesian network where each module contributes a likelihood factor to the overall inference model. GSE models provider state transitions via a finite-state automaton, where each category implies a distinct set of operational rules. The system enforces a dual constraint: modules must pass licensing gates and meet evidence standards before being admitted. Failure modes include revoked licenses (T6), unapproved crawling (non-GATED), and misclassification of data type (category mismatch). Dualities emerge in that T1/T2 modules support high-confidence decisions while T5/T6 modules are restricted to editorial use. The system avoids ad-hoc ingestion by enforcing a structured admission pipeline.
